A working group drafted proposals in 2024 to amend the laws on foreigners, on their integration and on state fees to stimulate the labour market. No source shows them adopted.

The Government reports a meeting of the working group at the State Tax Service with migration, health insurance, social insurance and public services bodies to stop several personal identification numbers being assigned to one foreigner. No source reports whether the problem was resolved.
The e-Governance Agency reports that the projects carried out over 15 years cost USD 46 million and that the savings from MPay alone recovered the investment. This is the agency's own account.

Government Decision No. 566/2025 allows technical, specialist and auxiliary posts in the public function to be filled by persons without Moldovan citizenship under employment contracts. The Commission confirms that these posts were opened to EU citizens while civil servant posts remain restricted.

The Government reports that after signing the agreement Moldovan authorities started a dialogue with the European Labour Authority on priority areas including EESSI. This is the Government's own account.

The Government reports that Moldova has concluded agreements on pension rights with Ukraine, Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan based on the territoriality principle. No source describes their application.
Law No. 595/1999 on international treaties is the basis on which the social insurance house negotiates and signs social security treaties.
The Government undertakes to fully transpose Directive 98/49/EC on supplementary pension rights. No source shows the transposition made.
A draft Presidential decree on starting negotiations of social security agreements appears only in the Government's plans.
A draft Government decision amending the Concept of the Social Protection information system appears only in the Government's plans.
A draft law on free access to employment for qualified nuclear personnel appears only in the Government's plans.
Interconnecting Moldova's social security system with those of EU Member States through EESSI appears only as a planned action. No source shows the connection made.
The Government lists aligning the data governance framework among its e-government priorities. No source shows a data governance framework or strategy adopted.
The Government plans to transpose all EU electronic communications acts by the end of 2027, starting with the Gigabit Infrastructure Regulation. No source reports completion.
The Government reports that Law No. 58/2024 amended sectoral laws to implement Law No. 48/2023 on cybersecurity.
The Government intends by 2027 to transpose the EU AI Act, develop a national AI law and designate or set up an institution for AI governance. No source shows the institution designated.
A draft Government decision approving the 2028-2030 implementation programme for the Digital Transformation Strategy appears only in the Government's plans.
A draft order amending the technical requirements for trust services appears only in the Government's plans.
A draft Government decision designating the National Coordination Centre for cybersecurity competence appears only in the Government's plans.
A draft Government decision on coordinated response to large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crises appears only in the Government's plans.
A draft Government decision amending Government Decision No. 211/2019 on MConnect appears only in the Government's plans.
Allocating two posts in the consumer protection inspectorate to advise consumers under the geo-blocking law appears only as a planned action.
Designating the national authority responsible for the law on data and data governance appears only as a planned action.
The Government plans to develop and implement the e-Legislation IT system. No source shows it in operation.

Law No. 195/2024, which entered into force in 2026, institutes the function of data protection inspector, and the Government notes that the data protection authority's capacity needs strengthening for it. No source shows inspectors appointed.
The Government plans an online public auction platform for confiscated assets. No source shows it developed.
A draft law on electronic invoicing in public procurement appears only in the Government's plans.
Reconfiguring the government public services portal to act as Point of Single Contact appears only as a planned action.
Designating operational officers for the EWRS platform appears only as a planned action.
The Government plans to create a Digital Transformation Unit in the Ministry of Health in 2026. No source shows it set up.
A draft order approving a methodology for processing and electronic exchange of health data appears only in the Government's plans.
A digital mechanism for access to personal data and consent management appears only as a planned action.

The only item gives a specific objective of the National Programme for Promoting Entrepreneurship on digitalising administrative processes, without stating when or whether the programme was approved or what it has delivered.
Piloting digital vouchers and an information system for agricultural day labourers is a planned Growth Plan action with a target of 6,000 registered workers. No source shows the pilot started.
Moldova plans to set up a national contact point for EPREL by December 2026. No source shows it set up.
Connecting the national tachograph card system to TACHOnet appears only as a planned action.
Government Decision No. 701/2014 approved the methodology for publishing open government data and is listed as part of the open data framework.
A Competition Council decision adopting a regulation on state aid for broadband networks was planned for August 2026. No source shows it adopted.

The National Council for Digitalisation, set up by ministry Order No. 165/2023, discussed and validated the digital transformation implementation programme. It appears to be the same body as the National Digital Transformation Council (INT-MDA-0532).
The Government lists MLearn among the reusable digital platforms developed and implemented. This is the Government's own account and no source gives figures on its use.
An annual implementation report on the Digital Transformation Strategy exists, and the Government notes that its baselines differ from those in the implementation programme.
The draft law on open data and reuse of public sector information was approved at the Government meeting of 19 March 2025 and sent to Parliament.
The draft was adopted by Parliament in May 2025 as Law No. 109/2025, partially transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1024 (see INT-MDA-0417).
Government Decision No. 376/2020 obliges public authorities to use only the MNotify service for electronic notifications and prohibits similar services. No source describes compliance with it.
The employment agency reports that an information campaign for refugees was organised with UNHCR support. No source describes its reach.
The employment agency reports that it monitored employers' notifications of employing Ukrainian citizens and vacancies for them each month. This is the agency's own account.
The employment agency's internal audit service carried out an engagement on how the EURES network is being implemented in Moldova. Its findings are not reported.
On 31 December 2025 the cadastre agency was still testing the Register of Utility Networks. No source shows it launched.
The draft Government decision amending the Concept of the State Register of Legal Units has been sent for approval at a Government meeting. No source shows it approved.
The EVOID mechanism is to be developed as the EVOSign enrolment flow is absorbed into the digital wallet. No source shows it in place.
The Government reports that the operating regulation of the Cybersecurity Agency's CERT directorate was drafted and approved.
The Government reports that an audit of the Real Estate Cadastre information subsystems and their security was launched on 20 November 2025. No source reports its results.
The Government Activity Programme 'EU, PEACE, DEVELOPMENT' was approved by Parliament Decision No. 269/2025 and includes a priority on integrating science, technology and data into governance.

The draft law on foreigners of February 2026 introduces a single residence card replacing the current documents for foreigners, with applications also possible electronically. No evidence item records the law adopted or the card issued.

The Government notes that the information systems of the employment agency and the social insurance house need to be adjusted and developed to be interoperable with EESSI. No source shows this work done.

The social insurance house lists the social security agreement with Belgium together with its administrative arrangement and forms. No source gives its date of entry into force or evidence of its application.

A draft agreement between Moldova and India on migration and mobility was under review, with the data protection authority asking for data protection provisions to be added. No source shows it signed.

A QR code on the digital medical leave certificate appears in a draft act, and the data protection authority asked for its access, data and security rules to be regulated explicitly. No source shows it introduced.
The data protection authority states that strengthening its preliminary complaint assessment procedure remains a priority. No source shows the change made.
The Cybersecurity Agency reports that Government Decision No. 824/2025 approved the regulation on coordinated vulnerability disclosure in cybersecurity.

The Cybersecurity Agency reports that it signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre in 2025, giving access to courses and technical support. This is the Agency's own account.
The Cybersecurity Agency reports that the methodological guide on cybersecurity measures for service providers in critical sectors is being drafted.
The Cybersecurity Agency reports cooperation with Lithuania covering PESCO projects and technical partnership, including on a DNS firewall. This is the Agency's own account and no results are given.
The new automated information system for the register of transport units and drivers is listed as under development. No source shows it launched.
The regulator reports that it set up a coordination mechanism with the main providers to apply Roam Like At Home and aligned their offers with the new rules. This is the regulator's own account.
The regulator reports that its Board decisions of April and November 2025 amended the rules on licence-exempt radio frequencies and equipment to harmonise with CEPT/ECC Recommendation ERC/REC 70-03.
The regulator reports that Board Decision No. 22 of 20 June 2025 amended its ex ante measures for the wholesale local access market.

The only item reports a study visit by the regulator to the Irish Safer Internet Centre in May 2025 in the context of transposing the Digital Services Act. No source shows a Safer Internet Centre planned or set up in Moldova.
The regulator plans to put a new regulation on end-user protection out for consultation in 2026 to harmonise with Law No. 72/2025.
The regulator presented its mobile services offers comparator among its digital consumer tools. No source gives figures on its use.
The Interoperable Europe factsheet states that Moldova is simplifying trade procedures for cross-border e-commerce with the EU but does not identify the measures or their status.
The Interoperable Europe factsheet describes the State Register of Controls as a central database recording planned and completed inspections and their results. No source gives figures on its use.

The Interoperable Europe factsheet reports that the Business Government Portal was launched in December 2020 as an extension of MCabinet and offers 11 data blocks for businesses. No source gives figures on its use.

The Interoperable Europe factsheet attributes the Cybersecurity Coordination Council to Government Decision No. 1186/2023, while the Government cites Government Decision No. 333/2024 for the Council (INT-MDA-0346). The status of Decision No. 1186/2023 cannot be confirmed from the sources.
The only item is a World Bank recommendation that Moldova's AI strategy align with the European Declaration on Digital Rights and Principles. No source shows any Moldovan step on the Declaration.
The ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 places Moldova in Tier 3, Establishing. This is an external assessment rather than a Moldovan measure, so an implementation status does not apply.
UNHCR recommends that Moldova continue providing legal work permits to refugees, which indicates that they are being provided. No source gives the number issued.

Research reports that Government Decision No. 115/2018 on the list of priority occupations, together with Law No. 200/2010, governs the right of residence for work and gives facilities to foreign workers in listed occupations. No source describes its application.

Disposition No. 4 of 1 March 2022 of the Commission for Exceptional Situations allowed Ukrainian citizens to be employed on fixed-term contracts during the state of emergency, with notification of the employment agency within five days. No source states whether it remains in force.

A Commission item states that Moldova joined the Roam Like At Home initiative, and the regulator reports rules under the roaming law and a coordination mechanism with providers to apply it. No source gives figures on its use.
